Sir,

In the Intelligence Report, dated December 6th 1939, reference was made to unrest existing among workers in the employ of the Aquarius Mineral Water Factory, 400, Thorburn Road.

Enquiries have since been conducted into the report, and it was learned that, on December 5th 1939, some 116 employees held a meeting in the office of the Japanese sponsored Chinese Workers Welfare Association, 127, Rangoon Road. During the meeting, it was decided that demands would be presented to the management of the company for an increase in wages ranging from 20% to 30%, and that nine dismissed workers be reinstated.

On December 7th 1939, the manager of the Aquarius Co., Mr. A. D. Openshaw, was interviewed. The gentleman stated that according to his knowledge no unrest existed among the workers, and that he did not anticipate trouble. However, it was learned from Mr. Openshaw that, on October 30th 1939, a letter had been received by the company, written on a letter-head of the Chinese Workers Welfare Association, 20, Canton Road. This letter was signed by one of the dismissed employees, one named Moo Zam Yuen ( 馬走元 ), and demanded the reinstatement of all such workers. The company gave no attention to the letter.

On the afternoon of December 8th 1939, a further letter was received by Mr. Openshaw, dated December 7th 1939, type-written in English, and signed by "The Whole Labourers." in which demands are made for:-

(1) A 40% increase for workers earning between $14.00 and $20.00 monthly.
(2) A 30% increase for workers earning between $20.00 and $30.00 monthly.

In response to the message, Det. Sergt. 88 Coleman,
Det. Sergt. 749 Urakami and C.D.S. 13 visited the
Aquarius Factory. Mr. Kearns informed the detectives
that the wife of the foreman, named Wong Zee Sz ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ),
had visited the factory and reported that her husband
had been arrested, beyond which nothing further was
known.

The wife was called to the station, and when
questioned, stated that at about 11 a.m. September
27th., 1939, two Japanese wearing the uniform of the
Japanese Military and a male Chinese civilian had
visited her home, at Lane 288, House 24, Yangchow Road,
detained her husband and driven him away in a motor
car (License Number Unknown).

Det. Sergt. Urakami communicated with Japanese
Military Police, Yangtszepoo Detachment Headquarters, 250,
Pingliang Road, and was informed that the foreman had
been called to the Divisional Headquarters for question-
ing, in connection with allegations made against him
by dismissed employees of the Aquarius Mineral Water
Factory.

接到消息后，88号警佐 Coleman、749号警佐 Urakami 以及 13号华籍侦探巡长前往宝华汽水厂。Kearns 先生告知侦探们，该工头的妻子 Wong Zee Sz（〔此处转录不清〕）曾到工厂报告其丈夫被捕，此外别无其他已知情况。

Urakami 警佐与位于平凉路250号的日本宪兵队杨树浦分队总部取得联系，获悉该工头因被宝华汽水厂解雇员工指控，已被召至区总部接受讯问。

Owing to lack of work following the approach
of the cool weather, the Aquarius Company Factory
(British), 400 Thorburn Road, has decided to dispense
with the services of some 130 casual workers. Some
80 of them have been discharged without incident.
It was planned to pay the remaining 50 men
off at 5.30 p.m. on September 15. They, however,
refused to accept the pay and demanded that they be
given work instead.
It is further learned that at about 5 p.m.
on September 14, some 20 of these workers called at
the Yangtsepoo Branch of the Chinese Workers' Welfare
Association, A.127 Rangoon Road, and requested
assistance in their demand for work. They were told
by a Japanese that they should appoint a representative
and their request would be given consideration.
Thereupon they elected one Ma Chao-yuin (馬趙雲),
residing in an unnumbered house on Pingliang Road, as
their representative.
At the request of the management, Police
from Yulin Road Station attended the factory at 5.30 p.m.

Sir:

At 4.45 p.m. September 15th., 1939, Mr. A.J. Openshaw, Manager, The Aquarius Mineral Water Factory, 400 Thorburn Road, telephoned to Yulin Road Station and requested Police assistance, as he was encountering a little trouble with his workers.

Det. Sergt. 88 Coleman, C.D.J. 235, . . . . 95 and the undersigned responded, and enquiries ascertained the following:-

For a number of years, the management of the Aquarius Mineral Water Factory have followed the system of employing some 100 to 130 temporary workers during the Summer Season. At the time they are engaged these casual labourers are already given to understand that the work is not permanent, and that their services would be dispensed with as soon as the Season ended.

The same procedure was followed during the present year, and already some seventy of these temporary workers have ceased to be employed, the firm encountering no trouble when they left.

A further 42 of the workers were under orders to cease on the night of September 15th., 1939, and during the past couple of days it was brought to the attention of the management that one of these temporary employees whose services were not being retained, named Moo Zau Yuen (馬趙元) 29, Tungchow, M/coolie, residing in a country house at Pingliang Road, employed in the Bottling Department, was agitating amongst the remainder of the employees whom it was proposed to dismiss.

88号警佐 Coleman，刑事司法登记号 235， ____ 95 以及本报告人随即出警，经查询查明如下情况：

多年来，Aquarius 矿泉水厂管理层一直实行在夏季雇佣约100至130名临时工的制度。在雇佣这些临时工时，已明确告知他们工作并非永久性质，一旦季节结束，他们的服务即被终止。

今年也沿用了同样的程序，目前已有约七十名此类临时工停止受雇，他们在离开时并未给公司带来任何麻烦。
